location: In the exercise the same inputs give features that differ by up to 4.4 between the two modes, and the head scores 51.9%, close to guessing.
finding: Unstated mechanism premise. The assertion that scoring 51.9% is 'close to guessing' relies on the unstated premise that the downstream evaluation task is a balanced binary classification problem where random chance is 50%. In a multiclass setting (e.g. 10 or 1,000 classes), 51.9% would be far above chance. The prose mentions only that the head is 'sized for yours' without defining the number of classes or expected baseline prior to evaluating the exercise.
evidence: Checked essay prose and exercise code. Section 'Freeze, train the head, then thaw' specifies only 'sized for yours'. Exercise lines 140 and 183 instantiate two-class linear layers ('nn.Linear(8, 2)') with balanced labels generated by thresholding two standard normal variables in 'target_batch()'.
fix: State in the prose that the downstream task is a balanced two-class problem: change to 'and on a two-class task the head scores 51.9%, close to guessing.'

location: What it cannot be is an accident. The same run took the old task from 99.4% to 53.4%.
finding: Ambiguous antecedent creates a misleading mechanism conclusion. The preceding paragraph contrasts three experimental conditions: letting buffers adapt (Option A, 98.5%), keeping them frozen (Option B, 80.6%), and thawing the backbone at a tenth of the head's learning rate (Thaw, 89.4%). Stating 'The same run took the old task from 99.4% to 53.4%' immediately following discussion of the thaw implies that thawing the backbone collapsed the original task. In fact, the thaw (which kept BatchNorm in eval mode) preserved old-task accuracy at 96.7%, whereas Option A (unfrozen buffers updating in train mode) was the run that caused the collapse to 53.4%.
evidence: Checked workspace/transfer-learning-freeze-then-thaw/exercise.py and corpus/transfer-learning-freeze-then-thaw/run.log. Option A reports 'old-task accuracy 0.534', whereas the thaw reports 'old-task accuracy 0.967'.
fix: Disambiguate 'The same run' to explicitly identify Option A: 'Letting the buffers drift on the new data (option A) took the old task from 99.4% to 53.4%.'

location: Layer normalisation keeps no buffers at all, so this drift cannot happen there.
finding: Technical term introduced without explaining the distinguishing mechanism. Layer normalisation is introduced in a single sentence at the close of the section without explaining why it has no buffers. To a reader moving into ML who has just learned that batch normalisation computes statistics over the mini-batch of m rows, stating that layer normalisation keeps no buffers leaves unexplained that layer normalisation normalises across features per sample rather than across the batch, eliminating the need for running cross-batch statistics.
evidence: Checked CONTEXT.md §1 ('one mechanism fully explained') and notes/BRIEF.md ('Explain necessary terms when first used'). The essay introduces Layer normalisation on line 87 without defining its axis of computation.
fix: Expand the sentence to explain the mechanism: 'Layer normalisation computes statistics across features within each individual sample rather than across the batch, so it keeps no buffers at all and this drift cannot happen there.'

location: ε is a tiny constant, 10−5 by default in PyTorch, that keeps the division safe when the variance is near zero.

location: Once the head is sensible, the second stage thaws the backbone and trains everything
finding: Anthropomorphism that obscures the mechanical condition. A neural network classifier head is a parameter tensor and does not possess good sense or become 'sensible'. The mechanical condition being described is that the head's weights have been updated so that its loss gradients have shrunk from their large initial values and stabilized.
evidence: Checked CONTEXT.md §4 ('No anthropomorphism that hides the mechanism... The word is allowed only when the next clause says what it stands for') and notes/BRIEF.md. Claim thaw-05 in receipts.tsv phrases the condition objectively: 'After the head has trained'.
fix: Replace 'Once the head is sensible' with 'Once the head has trained' or 'Once the head's gradients have stabilized'.
